from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP

def round_money(amount: str) -> str:
    """
    Round a decimal amount given as a string to two decimal places,
    rounding halves away from zero (ROUND_HALF_UP). Return the result
    as a string with exactly two decimal digits. Never return "-0.00".
    """
    # Convert to Decimal for precise arithmetic
    d = Decimal(amount)

    # Round to two decimal places using ROUND_HALF_UP
    rounded = d.quantize(Decimal('0.01'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)

    # Convert to string with exactly two decimal places
    result = f"{rounded:.2f}"

    # Avoid negative zero
    if result == "-0.00":
        result = "0.00"

    return result

import pytest
from solution import round_money

# Basic rounding to two decimals
def test_simple_no_fraction():
    assert round_money("2") == "2.00"
    assert round_money("-3") == "-3.00"

def test_one_decimal_place():
    assert round_money("2.5") == "2.50"
    assert round_money("-2.5") == "-2.50"

# Half‑away‑from‑zero behavior
def test_half_away_from_zero_positive():
    assert round_money("0.125") == "0.13"
    assert round_money("1.235") == "1.24"
    assert round_money("123.455") == "123.46"

def test_half_away_from_zero_negative():
    assert round_money("-0.125") == "-0.13"
    assert round_money("-1.235") == "-1.24"
    assert round_money("-123.455") == "-123.46"

# Edge of rounding boundary (exact .005)
def test_exact_half_boundary():
    assert round_money("0.005") == "0.01"
    assert round_money("-0.005") == "-0.01"

# Negative zero must be avoided
def test_negative_zero_handling():
    # -0.004 rounds to -0.00 but should be returned as 0.00
    assert round_money("-0.004") == "0.00"
    # -0.0001 also rounds to -0.00 -> 0.00
    assert round_money("-0.0001") == "0.00"

# Very large numbers (beyond typical float range)
def test_large_numbers():
    large = "12345678901234567890.125"
    assert round_money(large) == "12345678901234567890.13"
    # Negative large
    large_neg = "-98765432109876543210.125"
    assert round_money(large_neg) == "-98765432109876543210.13"

# Very small numbers (many leading zeros)
def test_small_numbers():
    assert round_money("0.0004") == "0.00"
    assert round_money("-0.0004") == "0.00"
    # 0.0049 should round up to 0.01
    assert round_money("0.0049") == "0.01"
    # -0.0049 should round down to -0.01
    assert round_money("-0.0049") == "-0.01"

# Input with explicit plus sign
def test_explicit_plus_sign():
    assert round_money("+2.5") == "2.50"
    assert round_money("+0.125") == "0.13"

# Input with surrounding whitespace
def test_whitespace_handling():
    assert round_money("  3.1415  ") == "3.14"
    assert round_money("\n-2.675\n") == "-2.68"

# Scientific notation input (Decimal supports it)
def test_scientific_notation():
    assert round_money("1e-2") == "0.01"
    assert round_money("-1e-2") == "-0.01"
    assert round_money("1.2345e2") == "123.45"
    assert round_money("-1.2345e2") == "-123.45"

# Very long fractional part (more than typical precision)
def test_long_fraction():
    # 0.123456789 rounds to 0.12
    assert round_money("0.123456789") == "0.12"
    # 0.125999 rounds to 0.13 (half up on the third digit)
    assert round_money("0.125999") == "0.13"
    # -0.125999 rounds to -0.13
    assert round_money("-0.125999") == "-0.13"

# Zero input variations
def test_zero_variants():
    for val in ["0", "0.0", "0.00", "-0", "-0.0", "-0.00", "+0", "+0.00"]:
        assert round_money(val) == "0.00"

# Invalid input should raise an exception (Decimal will raise)
def test_invalid_input():
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        round_money("abc")
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        round_money("")
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        round_money("1.2.3")
